text: In carpentry, sanding is an essential step before any cutting or sawing. Sanding smoothens rough surfaces, removing chips and scratches, and preparing the wood for further processing. After sanding, craftsmen often move on to sawing, cutting larger pieces from the wood. This method of cutting can be used for framing, paneling, or other construction tasks, allowing for precise and uniform material. Once the wood is sawed to the desired size, the carpenter can finish the piece with appropriate finishing techniques, such as planing or staining, before final assembly and use.
